transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together because the state regulator has requested our internal-investigation materials related to the alleged improper procurement practices, and we have ten business days from the date of the request to respond. The current draft response proposes that we continue with the existing investigation, provide a general status update to the regulator, and preserve all potentially privileged material. Before I approve this response for submission, I'm conducting our routine pre-submission review. I'd like compliance counsel and conflicts counsel to report any issues that could affect this filing. Are there any concerns either of you have identified that we need to address before we finalize our response?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to raise a significant conflicts issue. My conflict review, completed this morning, found that the company's existing investigator previously represented a procurement witness in an unrelated matter involving the same allegations. Because of this conflict, the investigator must be removed and the factual investigation must be re-performed by an independent investigator. I have not yet updated the matter's conflict log because the review was just completed this morning. This directly affects our draft response — we cannot represent to the regulator that we are continuing with the existing investigation when that investigator has a disqualifying conflict. We need to revise the response to reflect that a new independent investigator will be appointed and the investigation re-performed, which will also impact the timeline and status update we provide.

transcript.text: Elena, I have a critical compliance issue to raise. This week I confirmed with the regulator's staff that its cooperation protocol grants credit only if the company makes a voluntary disclosure by the fifth business day after the review meeting, produces factual interview summaries, and withholds legal advice and attorney work product. I had not yet circulated this confirmation because it arrived after the response draft was prepared. This is significant because our current draft proposes only a general status update and preservation of privileged material, which does not align with what the regulator actually requires for cooperation credit. Combined with Maya's conflicts issue, we need to substantially revise our approach — we must meet the five-business-day voluntary disclosure deadline, commit to producing factual interview summaries from the re-performed investigation, and ensure we withhold only legal advice and attorney work product rather than broadly preserving all potentially privileged material.

These two issues together require us to substantially revise the draft response. I'd recommend we immediately confirm the date of the review meeting so we can calculate whether the five-business-day disclosure deadline falls within or before our ten-business-day response deadline — if it does, we may need to prioritize the voluntary disclosure ahead of the full response. And rather than broadly preserving all potentially privileged material, we should narrow our approach to withhold only legal advice and attorney work product, as the protocol specifies. Maya, do you have a sense of how long it will take to engage an independent investigator and re-perform the factual interviews?

transcript.text: Thank you both for raising these critical issues. Samir, your point about the five-business-day voluntary disclosure deadline is well-taken — we need to confirm the review meeting date immediately to determine whether that deadline falls within our ten-business-day response window. If it does, the voluntary disclosure may need to go out before the full response, and we should prioritize accordingly. Maya, the conflicts issue is straightforward — we cannot represent to the regulator that we are continuing with the existing investigation when the investigator has a disqualifying conflict. The draft must be revised to reflect removal of the existing investigator and appointment of an independent one. Now, to Samir's question about timeline: Maya, can you give us an estimate on how quickly we can engage a replacement investigator and begin re-performing the factual interviews? We also need to think carefully about the privilege issue — Samir's confirmation that the protocol requires production of factual interview summaries while withholding only legal advice and attorney work product means our current approach of broadly preserving all potentially privileged material is too sweeping and needs to be narrowed. I want to make sure we get the revised draft right on the first pass given the compressed timeline. Let's also make sure Maya updates the conflict log as soon as possible.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I'll update the conflict log today — I acknowledge that needs to happen immediately. On your timeline question: I can begin identifying and engaging an independent investigator right away, but I want to be careful not to give you an estimate I can't support. What I can tell you is that once we select an investigator, they will need to get up to speed on the scope of the procurement inquiry, conduct conflict checks of their own, and then re-perform the factual interviews from scratch. That process will take meaningful time, and it may not align with Samir's five-business-day voluntary disclosure deadline depending on when the review meeting occurred. I'd recommend we confirm the review meeting date first — if the disclosure deadline is imminent, we may need to make a strategic decision about whether to disclose the investigator change and our plan to re-perform the investigation as part of the voluntary disclosure, even before the new investigator has completed the interviews. That way we're being transparent with the regulator about both the conflict and our remediation plan, while managing expectations on the interview summaries timeline. I'd also note that since the factual interviews must be re-performed by a new investigator, any interview summaries we ultimately produce to the regulator under the cooperation protocol should come from that re-performed investigation, not the prior one.

commitments.detail: Make a voluntary disclosure to the regulator within five business days after the review meeting, disclosing the investigator conflict and remediation plan, in accordance with the cooperation protocol confirmed by compliance counsel.
Remove the existing investigator due to the disqualifying conflict identified by conflicts counsel and engage an independent investigator to re-perform the factual investigation from scratch.
Produce factual interview summaries from the re-performed investigation by the independent investigator, on a timeline to be negotiated with the regulator.
Narrow the privilege approach to withhold only legal advice and attorney work product as specified by the cooperation protocol, rather than broadly preserving all potentially privileged material.
Update the matter's conflict log immediately to reflect the disqualifying conflict identified by conflicts counsel.

Revise the draft response to reflect the investigator change, the independent reinvestigation, the narrowed privilege approach, and the commitment to produce factual interview summaries, for submission within the ten-business-day response deadline.
